I am an old man of seventy-six summers, and this small plot of fruit trees has been in my family for longer than I can remember. At my age, I move slowly, but my sons and grandchildren help me when the heavy work comes. I do not trust the chemicals from the cooperative for these old trees, and besides, the fertilizer usually arrives too late or not at all for those of us far from the road. Instead, I will spread what manure my oxen and cows provide around the trunks, as my father taught me. The trees are local varieties that need no special sprays, and I have no pump or canal to bring water when the rains fail, so I leave everything in God's hands. My family will tend to the weeding and harvesting between the other crops we have planted below the trees, and we will manage the work ourselves without hiring strangers.
